llm.summary: This package appears to be a local Virtuoso Skill API lookup/linting tool (no network calls), but there are multiple inconsistencies (missing/mismatched database filenames, hard-coded local paths, and conflicting API counts) that warrant caution before running it on sensitive systems.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (API query, code linting, completion for Cadence Virtuoso Skill) aligns with the included scripts (chatbot, linter, parsers). However there are mismatches: the repo contains references/skill_api_database.json (312 functions) but key scripts expect files named skill_api_database.json or skill_api_database_full.json in other locations. The skill_lint.py docstring even claims a 10124-function DB while the included JSON metadata lists 312. These inconsistencies mean the provided files and what the scripts expect are not fully coherent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the provided scripts (chatbot, lint) which operate on local files and directories — expected. But scripts contain hard-coded input paths (e.g. /root/.openclaw/qqbot/downloads/CadenceSkillAPIFinder_1773394844827.html) and assume generation/placement of skill_api_database_full.json. Running the provided scripts as-is may read local files at those paths. The instructions do not mention the need to generate the full DB or the hard-coded path, which could lead to unexpected local file reads.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only), and all code is plain Python scripts included in the package. This is lower-risk than downloading arbitrary executables, but the presence of executable scripts means users will be running code from this package — review before execution. The web mode requires Flask (prompted by the code) and would need pip install flask if used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no special config paths. The scripts operate on local files and arguments only; there are no obvious requests for unrelated secrets or external tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show no special persistence privileges (always:false). The package does not request to modify other skills or global agent settings. It runs as ordinary scripts when invoked.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing or running this skill:
- Do not run the scripts on sensitive directories or as root without inspection; skill_lint.py will recursively read files you point it at and extract function calls.
- Verify the API database files expected by the scripts exist and match what you expect: skill_chatbot.py looks for skill_api_database.json by default, while skill_lint.py expects skill_api_database_full.json in the scripts directory. The repo provides references/skill_api_database.json — confirm whether you need to generate or rename files before use.
- Inspect the referenced JSON (references/skill_api_database.json) to confirm it only contains documentation data and no embedded secrets or unexpected fields.
- Note hard-coded paths in extract_functions.py and parse_api_data.py (e.g. /root/.openclaw/qqbot/downloads/...). These will try to read local files at those locations if you run those scripts without editing them. Remove or change hard-coded paths to known safe files before running.
- The web UI uses Flask. If you enable --web, ensure the server binds to localhost only (or run behind an appropriate firewall) and that you understand which port it will listen on; otherwise it may expose the UI to the network.
- Because the package contains executable Python scripts, run them in a controlled environment (isolated VM or container) until you confirm behavior and file dependencies. If you want to proceed, consider editing paths and filenames in the scripts so they point to explicit, safe files rather than implicit default locations.
- If you need stronger assurance, ask the publisher for a clear README describing the exact workflow to generate/load the DB, and for clarification about the differing API counts (312 vs 10124) and the expected database filenames/locations.
